title: Text someone you haven't talked to in a month. Just: “thought of you.”
why: Tiny reach-outs keep friendships alive through busy years.

title: Reply to the message you've been meaning to answer. Imperfect is fine.
why: An unanswered message quietly costs closeness. A quick reply wins it back.

title: Send a voice note instead of a text to one friend today.
why: Hearing a voice builds more closeness than reading words.

title: Ask a coworker one real question: “What's been the best part of your week?”
why: Small, sincere questions are how acquaintances start becoming friends.
evidence: Huang et al. 2017 (question asking and liking)

title: Call a family member and ask them something you've never asked before.
why: Curiosity turns a routine call into a real conversation.

title: Invite one person to a 20-minute coffee or walk this week. Name the day.
why: Friendships grow from time together, and a specific plan is far likelier to happen.

title: Tell a friend one specific thing you appreciate about them.
why: Appreciation strengthens a friendship more than most people expect.

title: Say yes to the next invitation you'd normally skip.
why: Showing up is most of friendship.

title: Host something small: three people, one easy dish or game. Send the invites today.
why: Being the one who gathers people is a skill anyone can learn.

title: Go to a class, club or meetup you've been curious about, and stay for the chat after.
why: Seeing the same faces again and again is how adult friendships form.

title: Share a song, photo or meme with someone it reminded you of.
why: “Saw this and thought of you” moments keep bonds warm with almost no effort.

title: Start a recurring thing with one friend: a weekly call or a monthly walk. Put the first one in both calendars.
why: Rituals carry friendships through the busy weeks.
